packageRules.description: Python dev/docs tooling: refresh the uv-compiled lock within the declared range. Auto-merge — the required CI checks are the gate; nothing from pip ships in the plugin. (update-lockfile keeps in-range bumps lock-only, but does NOT stop a range-widening PR when the newest version is ABOVE the declared ceiling — that case is covered by the allowedVersions cap below and the no-major-auto-merge rule.)

Deliberate tight version ceiling: ruff is capped on a standing policy — 0.x minors may ship new lint rules — rather than on an observed break. The cap itself is the allowedVersions below, and it is the only copy of the number here: allowedVersions stops Renovate from even proposing a version above it; without it, update-lockfile still raises a *minor* range-widening PR that would auto-merge. KEEP IN SYNC with requirements-dev.txt.
npm + GitHub Actions: auto-merge minor/patch/digest; majors are left for human review.

Toolchain versions (node, pnpm, python, uv, deno) are pinned and cross-file-coupled: each appears in mise.toml AND in frontend/package.json's packageManager and/or the workflow setup-* version inputs, and all copies must match (python = Decky's embedded libpython3.11, uv pinned for lock reproducibility, pnpm = packageManager, node = CI). Disabled by NAME across every manager so a bot bump can't desync one copy. The setup-* action SHAs themselves stay updatable (different dep names).

Never auto-merge a major update, in any ecosystem — a major dep bump (or, for pip, raising a `<next-major` ceiling such as pytest <10.0) always gets human review. Overrides the manager auto-merge rules above for major updates; minor/patch/digest and lock-file maintenance still auto-merge.
